newsitem.title: UK: BA ground staff union says seeks talks.
newsitem.headline: BA ground staff union says seeks talks.

text.p: British Airways Plc plc's ground staff have elected to seek further talks over sale of the airline's catering operation at London Heathrow Airport, effectively lifting the threat of strike, a spokesman for the main transport union said on Monday.

"The caterers have decided to seek further talks, which effectively means the threat of strike action is lifted for the present," Andrew Murray, a spokesman for the Transport and General Workers' Union (T&G) said.

The spokesman said the catering staff would almost certainly need to hold another strike ballot if they wanted to organise a walkout in the future. Unions are obliged to take action within 28 days of a strike ballot and must give the company seven-days notice.
The 1,400 catering workers, members of the T&G, last week rejected company proposals aimed at protecting their terms and conditions after the sale of the unit.
The sale is part of the airline's overall drive to sharpen its competitiveness by saving around one billion pounds by 2000 in several areas of its business.

Hundreds of BA's aircraft were grounded and thousands of passengers left stranded last week during a 72-hour cabin crew strike over pay and conditions. BA expects to hold talks with leaders of the 9,000 cabin crew later this week to try and resolve their dispute.

The separate confrontation between BA and its catering staff would have drawn baggage handlers and check-in staff into any strike action, with the likely result being further widespread disruption to the airline's operations, industry observers said.
BA shares were trading at 687-1/2p by 1507 GMT, down six pence on last Friday's level.
